briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with Iran asserting full control and threatening to block passage without its explicit permission, while the US unequivocally claims total dominance. Concurrently, escalating settler violence in the West Bank has prompted Israel to deploy additional forces and draw condemnation from the US Ambassador, underscoring severe internal and external pressures.

IRAN
Iran maintains its assertive stance on the Strait of Hormuz, with the spokesman for the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, Foreign Minister Araghchi, and Basij Chief Hossein Taeb all reiterating that no vessel can pass safely without Iranian authorization. Araghchi warned the US against "even bigger miscalculation" regarding the Strait, accusing American intelligence of repeated failures. Hamas publicly endorsed Iran's vow to keep the Strait closed until a regional ceasefire is achieved. Conversely, President Trump declared total US control over Hormuz, describing the naval blockade as a "wall of steel" and dismissing Iran's naval and air capabilities. Unconfirmed reports from Yahoo News and other sources claim the UAE released billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets, including 1.5 tons of gold, on August 11-12, potentially linking this to Iran's exemption of the UAE from recent attacks, though the UAE previously denied similar reports.

Internally, Iran faced significant economic challenges, as a trial program to dramatically increase gas prices in Kerman to 87,200 Toman/liter (a 1644% increase) was implemented and then swiftly halted due to reported public backlash and traffic at gas stations. Economic advisor Sadegh Hosseini advocated for "shock therapy" for price increases. The government continues its crackdown on dissent, with Iran International reporting 42 businesses closed in 17 cities for non-compliance with hijab laws. The EU and several other countries jointly condemned Iran's 916 executions in 2026 (15 in August) and its repression of protestors, calling for an immediate halt. Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani visited Baghdad, urging pro-Iranian militias to retain their weapons as leverage against Washington. Iran's Foreign Ministry denounced Israeli claims over the Golan Heights, affirming it as an "inseparable part of Syria."

ISRAEL
The Israeli Defense Ministry announced the successful reception of thousands of tons of military equipment, including D9 bulldozers, Humvees, JLTVs, and Oshkosh trucks, at Haifa Port, aimed at enhancing the operational readiness of ground forces. In the West Bank, Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir dispatched an additional infantry battalion to Qusra to address ongoing settler provocations and attacks against Palestinians, instructing troops to clarify rules of engagement. This move followed condemnation from US Ambassador Mike Huckaby, who labeled the actions of "Israeli terrorists" in Qusra as criminal and horrifying, stating Israeli forces intervened at US request. Illegal outposts in Qusra and Jalud (Area B) were dismantled by Golani Brigade 51, with one Israeli detained.

In Gaza, the IDF conducted airstrikes in Khan Younis, targeting a Hamas company commander, and in Beit Lahiya, targeting a Hamas cell leader planning attacks, resulting in at least two reported Palestinian fatalities. Paratroopers also shot a "terror operative" who crossed the "Yellow Line" in southern Gaza. Defense Minister Israel Katz affirmed an instruction for the IDF to prepare for a "long-term stay" in security areas across Gaza, Lebanon, and Syria, vowing not to retreat and to continue destroying Iranian-funded terror infrastructure. Domestically, the Tel Aviv District Court upheld a restrictive order against crime boss Yossi Musli. Discussions for the upcoming 26th Knesset elections are underway, with the Supreme Court deliberating on the eligibility of sitting Likud MKs/ministers in the party primaries scheduled for next week.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, Israeli airstrikes in Khan Younis and Beit Lahiya targeted Hamas commanders and operatives, with Palestinian media reporting at least two fatalities. IDF paratroopers in southern Gaza shot a "terror operative" who crossed the "Yellow Line" and posed an immediate threat. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported that Palestinians returning to Gaza are facing physical violence, threats, and humiliating treatment by Israeli soldiers at the Karam Abu Salem and Rafah crossings, noting that over half of Gaza's population lacks sufficient access to water, sanitation, and hygiene. The Gaza health ministry stated over 5,400 Palestinians have been killed or wounded since the US-backed "peace plan" and ceasefire process began in October 2025. Hamas declared its readiness to participate in elections as part of a "broad national coalition" and hailed Iran's call for a regional ceasefire.

The West Bank saw significant unrest, particularly in Qusra village, where Israeli settlers continued to besiege Palestinian homes. The IDF destroyed two illegal outposts in Qusra and Jalud in Area B and deployed an additional infantry battalion to maintain order. US Ambassador Mike Huckaby strongly condemned the settler actions as criminal and terrifying, attributing the IDF's intervention to a US request. The EU also called for an end to settler violence and accountability for perpetrators. More than 300 Israeli reserve soldiers petitioned IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir to address "Jewish terrorism" by settlers. Renewed settlement activity was noted in Ganim, 20 years after its evacuation.

LEBANON
An explosion attributed to IDF forces was reported in Majdal Zoun, southern Lebanon, and Israeli forces were documented demolishing homes and infrastructure using explosives in Mansouri. A Lebanese woman in Sohmor vowed steadfastness despite widespread destruction from Israeli strikes. Reuters reported that Israel and Lebanon have agreed on Britain, Italy, Switzerland, and Indonesia to contribute troops to an international mechanism verifying Hezbollah's disarmament under a US-mediated framework. This mission would involve inspecting villages in southern Lebanon, with Israel pushing for private homes to be included. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam's account reportedly had a tweet condemning Israeli raids, which was later deleted, with claims of account hacking. Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz reiterated that Israel "will not retreat from security zones" in Lebanon and other areas, stating it's Israeli policy to continue destroying terror infrastructure.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Iranian Foreign Ministry reaffirmed the occupied Golan Heights as an "inseparable part of Syria" and condemned Israeli claims of sovereignty, with Syria having filed a complaint against Colombia for its recognition of Israeli control. Unverified reports claimed Joulani gangs fired mortars and heavy weapons on the Syrian-Lebanese border under the guise of military training.

In Iraq, Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani reportedly visited Baghdad, meeting with pro-Iranian militias and leadership, urging them to retain their weapons to exert pressure on Washington. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reiterated that the September 30 deadline for the withdrawal of foreign forces from Iraq is "final and irreversible." Zaidi also stated that Iraq would not allow its territory or airspace to be used for attacks against neighboring countries and met with CENTCOM leadership to discuss a shift towards economic, development, and security cooperation. A high-level Iraqi security delegation arrived in Saudi Arabia to discuss joint security issues. The Iraqi Oil Marketing Company (SOMO) confirmed that a leading Abu Dhabi energy company is buying Iraqi crude and shipping it via the Strait of Hormuz. Reports indicated an increased pace of US convoys withdrawing from Iraqi Kurdistan towards neighboring countries.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia is reportedly considering backing a Yemeni ground offensive to retake the Red Sea coast from the Houthis, following a Houthi ballistic missile attack on the commercial vessel *Tihamah*. The Houthis, in turn, threatened to target Saudi oil fields, airports, and electricity/water infrastructure if a comprehensive war erupts. Saudi oil tankers are reportedly rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope to avoid Houthi threats, leading to a halt in operations for most Red Sea tankers, with over a dozen empty tankers heading to Omani and Emirati ports. A high-level Iraqi security delegation arrived in Saudi Arabia to discuss security files. The Turkish Defense Ministry announced upcoming joint military drills with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan focused on defense industry co-production.

Unconfirmed reports from Yahoo News and "kianmeli1" claim the UAE released billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets, including 1.5 tons of gold, on August 11-12, alleging this to be the third such transfer. This is speculated to be a reason Iran exempted the UAE from recent attacks, though the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs previously denied similar reports. Oman was chosen by Iran's Tractor SC as its host for AFC Champions League Elite matches. Ambrey maritime security firm reported participating in a rescue operation for a tanker in distress off the coast of Oman. Bahraini authorities reportedly continue arbitrary arrests and enforced disappearances of the Shia majority population.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Hormuz Standoff Intensifies:** Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya, Foreign Minister Araghchi, and Basij Chief Hossein Taeb all asserted Iran’s full control over the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran stating no vessel can pass safely without its permission. This directly contrasts with US President Trump's declaration of total US control over the Strait, calling their naval blockade a "wall of steel."
2.  **West Bank Settler Violence & IDF Response:** Israeli settlers continued to besiege Palestinian homes in Qusra. The IDF destroyed two illegal outposts in Qusra and Jalud (Area B) and IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir dispatched an additional infantry battalion to Qusra, also instructing troops to clarify rules of engagement. US Ambassador Mike Huckaby condemned the "Israeli terrorists" in Qusra.
3.  **Gaza Operations:** The IDF conducted airstrikes in Khan Younis and Beit Lahiya, targeting Hamas commanders/operatives, resulting in at least two reported Palestinian fatalities. Paratroopers also shot an operative crossing the "Yellow Line" in southern Gaza.
4.  **Iranian Asset Release by UAE (Unconfirmed):** Yahoo News and other sources reported that the UAE released billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets, including 1.5 tons of gold (approx. $212 million), on August 11-12. This is alleged to be the third such transfer, possibly linked to Iran exempting the UAE from recent attacks.
5.  **Iraqi Sovereignty & Militias:** Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani visited Baghdad, instructing pro-Iranian militias to retain their weapons. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reiterated a "final and irreversible" September 30 deadline for foreign forces to withdraw and stated Iraq would not allow its territory or airspace to be used for attacks against neighbors.
6.  **Internal Iranian Gas Price Crisis:** A trial program in Kerman to drastically raise gas prices to 87,200 Toman/liter (1644% increase) was swiftly implemented and then halted due to public outcry and queues at gas stations, highlighting economic instability.
7.  **Israeli Military Build-up:** The Israeli Defense Ministry announced the arrival of thousands of tons of military equipment, including D9 bulldozers and armored vehicles, at Haifa Port to strengthen ground forces. Defense Minister Katz declared a "long-term stay" for the IDF in security zones across Gaza, Lebanon, and Syria.
8.  **Yemen-Saudi Escalation:** The Houthis threatened to target Saudi oil fields, airports, and infrastructure if a comprehensive war erupts, while Saudi Arabia is reportedly considering a ground offensive to retake the Red Sea coast from the Houthis.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high in the Strait of Hormuz due to conflicting claims of control by Iran and the US, with any incident having the potential to trigger broader military confrontation. The unverified report of Iranian missile launches towards ships in Hormuz, if true, would represent a severe escalation. West Bank instability is critical, with ongoing settler violence necessitating significant IDF intervention and drawing strong international condemnation. The Yemen-Saudi conflict carries a medium risk of escalation, potentially disrupting global energy markets further should Houthi threats to Saudi infrastructure materialize or a Saudi ground offensive proceed. Internally, Iran faces a medium threat of social unrest due to high inflation, economic pressures highlighted by the failed gas price hike, and ongoing crackdowns on dissent. Military postures include Iran asserting defensive and offensive capabilities, the US maintaining a naval blockade and preparing for potential prolonged reduced embassy staffing, and Israel enhancing its military equipment and committing to long-term presence in regional security zones.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US, through President Trump, affirmed absolute control over the Strait of Hormuz and strongly condemned settler violence in the West Bank via Ambassador Huckaby. The State Department is preparing US embassies in the Middle East for extended reduced staffing. The EU, alongside Canada, the UK, and numerous European nations, issued a joint statement condemning Iran's executions and repression, demanding an immediate halt. Russia's President Putin visited the disputed Kuril Islands, prompting Japan to summon the Russian Ambassador, while Russia's Medvedev issued a stark warning to Japan. Turkey is scheduled to conduct joint military drills with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. Iraq's Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reiterated a firm September 30 deadline for foreign forces to withdraw and stated Iraq's commitment not to be used as a base for attacks against neighbors.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding control of the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran and the US presenting diametrically opposed narratives. The claim of Iranian missiles being fired at ships in Hormuz (kianmeli1) is unverified and lacks corroboration from any other source, suggesting potential disinformation. Similarly, unconfirmed reports of the UAE releasing billions in frozen Iranian assets (including gold) conflict with previous UAE denials and require independent verification. The rapid implementation and reversal of the gas price hike in Kerman highlight a fluid and sensitive internal situation in Iran, susceptible to misinformation and propaganda. Propaganda indicators include Iranian rhetoric about a "dirty nuclear bomb" and a NAYA report disparaging Emirati military recruitment, likely intended for psychological impact. There is a reporting gap regarding the specifics of the "US-backed 'peace plan' and ceasefire process in October 2025" mentioned in relation to Gaza casualties, making it challenging to fully contextualize this claim.
